title: Manus, Father of the Abyss
snippet: His immense mass of humanity out of control led to the manifestation of an Abyss that spread, threatening to devour the entire land. The Dark emanating from Manus generated countless Humanity Phantoms and seeped among the residents of Oolacile, making their humanity go wild and mutating their bodies, their bloated heads lined with innumerable tiny red eyeballs and brain parts protruding from cracks. Corrupted Oolacile sorcerers discovered abyssal sorceries, more weighty and dealing physical damage instead of magical, since the Dark produced sorceries with a more tangible, "human" presence.

title: Knight Artorias
snippet: Kaathe, following his failure with the Four Kings, arrived in Oolacile and manipulated its inhabitants into upturning the grave of Manus, a primordial man with an extraordinary Dark Soul and dark sorcery skills, who had been buried beneath the dungeons of their city, and resurrect him. Awakening to find his precious broken pendant missing, Manus was eventually driven mad and his Dark Soul went wild, transforming him into a dark beast eternally seeking his pendant. His immense mass of humanity out of control led to the manifestation of an Abyss that spread, threatening to devour the entire land. The Dark emanating from Manus not only generated countless Humanity Phantoms with a will of their own but also influenced the residents of Oolacile, making their humanity go wild and horribly mutating their bodies, bloating their head and opening them with cracks lined with innumerable tiny red eyeballs and protruding brain parts.

title: Manus, Father of the Abyss
snippet: Manus was a sorcerer of Oolacile, and after he died, his body was buried in the caverns beneath the city. 200 to 300 years prior to the journey of the Chosen Undead, the Primordial Serpent Kaathe arrived in Oolacile, in search of a potential Dark Lord following the flooding of New Londo. He manipulated the country to upturn the grave of the primordial man, Manus, buried beneath the dungeons of their city and resurrect him. Manus awakened to find his pendant missing, and was eventually driven into a beastly frenzy as his Dark Soul went wild, transforming him into the "Father of the Abyss".

title: Manus, Father of the Abyss
snippet: Manus at one point kidnapped Princess Dusk of Oolacile—possibly after her rescue from a Golden Crystal Golem—and imprisoned her deep within the Chasm of the Abyss. In the meantime, his prized pendant came under the possession of Seath the Scaleless and then a Chosen Undead in the future; Manus, driven by his unrelenting search for his pendant, snatched the Undead from the future and brought them into the old Oolacile. There, the Chosen Undead put down the corrupted Knight Artorias and journeyed within the Chasm of the Abyss, where they finally defeated Manus and put him to rest. While Dusk was rescued in the process, she was driven by Elizabeth into thinking that she was saved by Artorias, preserving the legacy of the Wolf Knight. Nevertheless, Dusk came to recognize the Chosen Undead's similarity to the fabled knight, and developed doubts of her own as to her true savior.

title: Oolacile
snippet:
Despite this, when returning to the current age and speaking to Dusk, she would simply note that the Chosen Undead looks a lot like Artorias (believing it was Artorias who rescued her from Manus), without expanding on whether or not the Chosen Undead's actions had any effect in saving Oolacile.

While speaking to Marvelous Chester, he would say that "Oolacile has brought the Abyss upon itself [...] Fooled by that toothy serpent, they upturned the grave of primeval man, and incited his ornery wrath", implying that either Kingseeker Frampt or Darkstalker Kaathe had a hand in Oolacile's downfall. Due to the inherent darkness of the Abyss, Darkstalker Kaathe is the more likely culprit.

title: Manus, Father of the Abyss
snippet: As the Abyss spread across the land of Oolacile, Knight Artorias arrived to halt its advance and confront Manus, as the Knight of Gwyn already had experience with fighting the Abyss and its creatures after the events of New Londo and his hunt for the Darkwraiths, and possessed a Silver Pendant that protected him from the Dark. However, Artorias's pendant was stolen by Oolacile's inhabitants and hidden behind an illusory wall, depriving Artorias of protection against Manus's dark sorceries. Together with his trusted companion Sif, Artorias faced Manus but his strength proved insufficient to defeat him, and he succumbed to the Abyss. Injured in the battle, Artorias used his Cleansing Greatshield to form a magic barrier that protected Sif from the Dark. Now corrupted to his soul by the Abyss and with his armor corroded, Artorias was left to fight alone and hold back the treacherous citizens of Oolacile.

title: Knight Artorias
snippet: As the Abyss continued to spread across the land of Oolacile, Knight Artorias arrived to halt its advance and confront Manus, as the Knight of Gwyn already had experience from fighting the Abyss and its creatures in New Londo. However, Artorias's silver pendant was stolen by Oolacile's inhabitants and hidden behind an illusory wall, depriving Artorias of protection against Manus's dark sorceries. Artorias, together with his trusted companion Sif, nevertheless faced Manus, but his strength proved insufficient to defeat the Father of the Abyss. Wounded in the battle, Artorias used his Cleansing Greatshield to form a magic barrier to protect Sif against the Dark. Artorias, his soul corrupted by the Abyss and his armor corroded, was left alone in his fight against the Abyssal creatures of Oolacile.

title: Knight Artorias
snippet:
Manus at one point kidnapped Princess Dusk of Oolacile and imprisoned her deep within the Chasm of the Abyss. title: Knight Artorias
snippet: The Abyss Watchers established dominion over Farron Keep, the swampland once known as Oolacile or Darkroot Garden. Here they closely guarded what was once the Chasm of the Abyss, the cradle of Manus and a seedbed for Abyssal beasts; these headquarters would also have been in close proximity to Artorias's tomb. The Watchers gained notoriety due to their scorched-earth approach to containing outbreaks of the Abyss, destroying kingdoms at the first sign of exposure. Nonetheless, many would enlist as their followers in a bid to partake of wolf's blood and become part of the Undead Legion.

title: Oolacile
snippet:
Oolacile -  Dark Souls - location - lead 
 lead : The lost land of **Oolacile** is a location that no longer exists by the events of *Dark Souls*. Several sources allude to its existence centuries beforehand and its focus on sorceries. Dusk of Oolacile states that the land "was reduced to ashes" long ago.

The later version of the game, *Dark Souls: Prepare to Die Edition*, comes with extra content that takes place in Oolacile 200-300 years before the events of the game, where the Chosen Undead must take the place of Artorias the Abysswalker and rescue Dusk from Manus, Father of the Abyss. During this period, Oolacile is slowly being swallowed by the Abyss. The content was later added as DLC to the console versions of the game as *Artorias of the Abyss*.

snippet:

 dark_souls_ii : Although he was killed, the Dark Soul of Manus was so large and powerful that he was reborn in death, and his soul split into miniscule fragments that retained some will. These pieces began to coalesce once again by absorbing other humanities, becoming the incarnations of different emotions of Manus and then human in shape, with their own self-awareness: Elana was the embodiment of Manus' wrath, Alsanna of his fear, Nadalia of his solitude and Nashandra, the tiniest fragment of Manus, the embodiment of his want. These new entities had some recollection of their father and his dark powers and when the Abyss that they called home was dissipated they scattered across the land. To sustain themselves and seek power, they reached Drangleic where in one way or another they came into contact with the holders of magnificent souls, drawn to their awesome strength.

title: Knight Artorias

The wolf inherited Artorias's divine greatsword and the magical ring that had allowed the knight to cross the Abyss. The wolf settled in the forest where Artorias's tomb had been erected and, wielding his companion's sword in his jaws, continued to fight to guard Artorias's rest, slaughtering the numerous Undead who arrived with the intention of plundering the tomb of the legendary knight.

While unaware that Artorias had been corrupted by the Abyss before he could save her, Dusk's senses do hint that the Chosen Undead bears the same "resonance" as her fabled savior, leading her to question the details of her temporarily intangible captivity.

title: Manus, Father of the Abyss
snippet:
Manus, Father of the Abyss -  Dark Souls - boss - trivia 
 trivia : Manus may be named for Mannus, the father of mankind in Germanic mythology. According to the Roman writer Tacitus, the Germanic tribes believed a god *Tuisto* sprang from the ground and had a son, *Mannus*, from whom all humans were descended. Manus is also the Latin word for “hand”, alluding to Manus’s massive left hand.
**However a more accurate translation of "深淵の主マヌス" would be "Manus, Lord of the Abyss".

title: Manus, Father of the Abyss
snippet:
Manus, Father of the Abyss -  Dark Souls - boss - notes 
 notes : The Silver Pendant, although not required, can be of great help as it blocks his magic attacks if used with correct timing.

Great Grey Wolf Sif can help in this battle. Whilst Sif's attacks are not very damaging, the extra summon can keep Manus distracted and give the player time to heal. It is wise to only summon Sif after Manus is below half health, to distract him in his harder phase, making it less likely the player will be targeted by the Dark Orb barrage attack.

Sif's summon sign is *inside* the Manus's arena, directly to the left of where the player spawns. As a result, Sif can only be summoned *during* the fight. Thankfully, Sif is summoned instantly after touching the sign, without the usual white phantom-summoning animation. Since it is summoned during the fight it does not increase Manus' Hp.

title: Artorias of the Abyss
snippet:
Artorias of the Abyss -  Dark Souls - mechanic - plot 
 plot : While everything about *Artorias of the Abyss* is technically optional, the main storyline consists of the Chosen Undead taking the place of Knight Artorias, rescuing Dusk of Oolacile and killing Manus, Father of the Abyss.

title: Humans
snippet: Meanwhile, in a place called Oolacile, the land of golden sorceries, humans loyal to the Gods were convinced by the Darkwraith leader named Kaathe, a primordial serpent loyal to the Pygmy, to raise up a primeval man who had been buried there. He went mad, and his Humanity bubbled over from his uncontrollable rage, mutating him into a dark monster. His Humanity overflowed and consumed the very world around him, generating another Abyss, and corrupting the citizens of Oolacile. Knight Artorias, one of the four knights of Gwyn, would be tasked to face the outbreak of the Abyss, only to be corrupted by it.

title: Chosen Undead
snippet: Finally, the Chosen Undead arrives at the Chasm of the Abyss where an illusion of Alvina guides the player to an illusory wall. Inside, the Chosen Undead discovers an injured Sif, protected by a magic barrier created by Artorias, in order to prevent Sif from being engulfed. Shortly after rescuing Sif the player faces Manus, Father of the Abyss, who is responsible for the spread of the dark. Manus is defeated, and Princess Dusk is saved. Upon returning to Oolacile Sanctuary, they are greeted by Elizabeth, who tells the Chosen Undead that she will let everyone know that Artorias was the one who defeated Manus, so that his honor may prevail. However, she assures them that their great deed will not be forgotten.

title: Giants (Lore)
snippet: Sometime around the fall of Oolacile, Gough arrived at the kingdom in response to the uncontrollable expansion of Manus' Abyss. However, he was imprisoned by the citizens of the country in a tower sealed by powerful magic. The eye holes of his helm were packed with tree resin by those who dismissed the force of the giant as brutish, indicating racist sentiments of many towards the giants.

title: Chosen Undead
snippet: After being dragged back in time, the Chosen Undead wakes up inside a cave beneath some trees. Outside, they are confronted by the Sanctuary Guardian. After slaying the beast, the Chosen Undead finds some sort of garden temple where they encounter a giant, talking mushroom named Elizabeth, who informs the player that the realm of Oolacile is being consumed by the darkness of the Abyss, She also tells the player that Princess Dusk has been kidnapped by a creature from the abyss and that Knight Artorias has ventured unto Oolacile to put an end to the spread. However, she assures the player that Artorias will be overwhelmed by the darkness.

title: Lords
snippet: Darkstalker Kaathe, who opposed Gwyn's actions, attempted to bring about the Age of Dark and the coming of its ruler, the Dark Lord; most travelling to Oolacile and manipulating the citizens into upturning the grave of "primordial man". This resulted in Oolacile's fall as it began to be swallowed by the Abyss, consuming the land and corrupting its citizens. Kaathe also went to New Londo, seducing the Four Kings with the art of lifedrain, which corrupted them and their knights. In an effort to contain his darkwraiths, New Londo was flooded -an act that ultimately cost the lives of the city's inhabitants.

title: The Nameless King
snippet: However, the rest of the firstborn's reign was marked by catastrophes. The Four Kings of New Londo were corrupted by the dark power of Darkstalker Kaathe, starting to sow devastation nearby the city of the gods. Following Knight Artorias's failure to defeat the Darkwraiths, the gods were forced to flood the city, sacrificing all the humans within, and seal it. A similar event happened in Oolacile when, again due to Kaathe, the awakening of the primordial human Manus and his fury led to the collapse of the country when Artorias was unable to defeat him. In addition to the grave situation on the borders of Anor Londo, the city of the gods itself became a dangerous place when a group of cultists began targeting the clan of Gwyn and their kind, and occult weapons capable of killing the gods reached inside the walls of Anor Londo. title: Drangleic
snippet: As the First Flame continued to wane, an Abyss opened beneath Drangleic, the result of the scattered fragments of an ancient abyss and the dissipated Manus, Father of the Abyss. Coalescing again, this abyss expanded across the region and assimilated all things into its growth, with its darkness felt even by those attuned to magic in neighbouring regions. A group of Undead led by Darkdiver Grandahl, called the Pilgrims of Dark, started to make pilgrimages to what they considered holy sites and delved into the Dark Chasm, to overcome the trials that lurked in the depths to refine the darkness within them. In the heart of the abyss, the Darklurker manifested: A dark, angelic creature that manipulated darkness along with sorcery, pyromancy and miracles and demonstrated superhuman abilities.

title: Primordial Serpents
snippet:
Kaathe resides in the darkness of the Abyss, but seems to be more involved in the affairs of Lordran than Frampt. Kaathe gave the Four Kings the art of lifedrain and consequently founded the Darkwraith covenant. He also seems to have tricked the residents of Oolacile into uncovering the corpse of Manus, driving him mad in the process. This sparked the spread of the Abyss, transforming the townsfolk into monstrous beings whose humanity has run wild, akin to Manus.

In the ending of Dark Lord, ten additional primordial serpents are seen, whose names are unknown. They appear to want to serve the newly-appointed Dark Lord, and possibly usher in the Age of Dark. An interesting note in this ending is that Kaathe states that both himself and Frampt will serve the Chosen Undead, disregarding any actions the player has taken before reaching this point, like placing the Lordvessel with Frampt instead of Kaathe, which would make the latter refuse to cooperate with the player, and vice-versa.

title: Abyss Watchers
snippet: Eventually, the Watchers linked the Fire, although it is unknown if one or all had done so. With the Watchers becoming Lords of Cinder, the wolf blood dried up. The Followers, now having nothing to live for, went hollow, roaming the land and eventually disappearing into the Painted World of Ariandel. With no one remaining to execute the corrupted, the acolytes were slowly devolved by the Abyss, and Farron was consumed in a rotting bog. When the Abyss Watchers were awakened to kindle the Flame once again, they returned home to find it corrupted and their mission unsuccessful. The Watchers in the keep now fight against themselves, endlessly slaying their brethren corrupted by the Abyss.

 dark_souls_iii : The time of Lothric wasn't kind to the forest-dwelling Mushroom People. For a time they lived in the forest of Farron, undisturbed, and were even regarded as divine beings by the Xanthous Scholars, researchers who wished to learn more about the lost country of Oolacile.

However, they would meet a rather violent end at the hands of the Ghrus, who emerged after the forest was consumed by a poisonous bog, a process that began when the Abyss Watchers linked the First Flame. What can be presumed to be the calcified remains of Elizabeth can also be found in a hidden cave containing the clothes of Princess Dusk and a scroll full of sorceries of Oolacile. It's unclear if some of the Mushroom People still exist far away from the rotted forest, or if they faced extinction after the Ghru's arrival.

snippet:

 dark_souls : During the events of *Dark Souls*, Oolacile is not a location that can be visited. The Enchanted Ember is described as "a vestige of the lost land of Oolacile". Dusk of Oolacile expands more on her home land during dialogue with the Chosen Undead, describing it as "the home of ancient sorceries". She explains that Oolacile's sorceries are more "of an approximation" when compared to those used by the Chosen Undead, but also reveals that she does not belong to this time and that Oolacile "was reduced to ashes" long ago.

The locations of both the Enchanted Ember and Dusk of Oolacile — in Darkroot Garden and Darkroot Basin respectively, as well as the Grave of Artorias located in Sif's boss area — imply that Oolacile was once located nearby. The maps of Darkroot Garden and Royal wood also have striking similarities.

title: Abyss
snippet: Knight Artorias famously traversed New Londo's Abyss and hunted the Darkwraiths therein. He was protected by the power of a magical ring, which he gained after making a covenant with the beasts there. The ring prevented him from being swallowed by the void, but it led to his sword becoming cursed. In recognition of his actions, he was awarded one of Anor Londo's treasures, a Silver Pendant that allowed him to repel Dark sorceries; eventually he traveled to Oolacile to combat the threat of Manus, the lord of the Abyss. He ultimately failed in his mission he was overtaken by the dark, leaving behind his companion Sif.

title: Abyss
snippet:
Abyss -  Dark Souls - location - location 
 location : In Dark Souls the Abyss is located at the end of the New Londo Ruins. To reach to the Abyss, the floodgates must be lowered and the Covenant of Artorias ring, a reward for killing Great Grey Wolf Sif, must be worn. After climbing down a spiral staircase within a tower, the path will abruptly end, making it necessary to descend into the darkness of the Abyss.

The DLC *Artorias of the Abyss* allows us to explore a more recent Abyss, despite being located in a past era, deep within the dungeons of Oolacile.

snippet:

In addition, the Manus Catalyst also boosts the power of Dark sorceries, based on the player's strength stat.
The strong attack of the Manus Catalyst is quite powerful for a catalyst, but very slow, and uses the Greataxe moveset.

title: Chosen Undead
snippet: During their quest in Oolacile the Chosen Undead also meets Marvelous Chester, a somewhat sinister merchant who, like the player, was dragged into the past. He reveals to the Chosen Undead that the spread of the dark was caused when the inhabitants of Oolacile opened the grave of the primeval man due to the influence of a "toothy serpent". The Chosen Undead then treads through Oolacile Township in search of the dark source.

title: Frozen Eleum Loyce
snippet: At some point Alsanna reached Eleum Loyce and became close to the Ivory King. She was in truth a fragment of the Dark Soul of Manus, Father of the Abyss, that, despite the fact that he had been killed centuries in the past, had retained some of his will and power. Alsanna was born as the incarnation of Manus' fears and despite being a frightened and frail thing she managed to to coalesce once again absorbing the other humanities, and then obtain the shape of a human, with her own self-awareness. To sustain herself and seek more power, she sought the holders of magnificent souls, drawn to their awesome strenght. Alsanna thus sought the Ivory King to sustain herself and smother her innate fear and was accepted by him, quietly finding a place at the side of the leader of Eleum Loyce where he provided her comfort and she accepted Eleum Loyce as her home.

title: Black Dragon Kalameet
snippet: However, at a certain point, a Chosen Undead who ended up in Oolacile challenged the black dragon and after a legendary battle managed to defeat him. From his tail they formed an Obsidian Greatsword infused with the mystical power of the dragon and with his orange eye they created an enchanted ring that doubled the damaged received by its wearer.

title: Elizabeth
snippet: After the successful rescue of Oolacile's crown princess, she thanks the hero, but decides against sharing the truth of the tale, leading the heroic deed to be associated with Artorias instead. She also refuses to elucidate Dusk on the true nature of the beast that had kidnapped her, despite her many requests.

title: Hawkeye Gough
snippet: He witnessed the fall of Oolacile caused by their arrogance and greed, as well as Artorias' failure to quell the Abyss and his demise at the hands of the Chosen Undead. Should the time traveling hero choose to engage the legendary Kalameet, a dragon so fierce not even Anor Londo dared to cross him, Gough could even be allowed one last hunt, firing an impressive shot in spite of his now limited vision, speaking to the true might of the legendary archer. Having done that, though, he'll give away his precious bow, officially leaving that life behind him.

title: Lords
snippet:
One of Gwyn's four knights, Artorias, and his wolf companion Sif made a covenant with the beings of the Abyss that allowed him to traverse it, so that he could hunt the Darkwraiths. Artorias later arrived in Oolacile in an attempt to combat the spread of the Abyss, but was overcome and was forced to sacrifice his greatshield to save Sif. This left him unprotected from the Abyss, and he later became corrupted and driven to madness.

The Way of White was usurped by Gwyn's uncle, Lloyd, who also would start hunts against the Undead.

Eventually, the undead were corralled into several asylums to await the end of the world, for it is prophesied by Astora - who themselves inherited the prophecy from Frampt - that one day an undead will escape the prison and succeed Gwyn in linking the fire. At the same time, Kaathe preaches that this chosen has the opportunity to become the new Dark Lord and usher in the Age of Dark.

title: Bastille Lord
snippet:
His fear became so vast and overwhelming that he quickly turned to worse methods to rid himself of the horrible blight. When the Bastille had become too full of afflicted humans, he ordered his monstrous Flexile Sentries to round up as many of them as possible into flimsy ships, to hurl them into the ocean and have them die at sea, away from land. Among them were the sorcerers of his country, some of which would survive the horrible punishment and find their way to a southern land where they established their own kingdom.

Despite all the measures he took to prevent his kingdom from falling victim to the fading of its era, the Bastille Lord could not stop the march of time. Olaphis would crumble into obscurity, and with the passage of time, the land would come to be known first as Venn, then as Drangleic. The ruins of his castle still stand, rotting away with some of its original, undying captives.

title: Lothric
snippet: The fading of the Flame and the erosion of their faith made the citizens of Lothric more and more desperate, some of whom were transformed into humanoid trees that were turned in prayer towards Lothric Castle. Furthermore, the undead of the city began to show signs of an epidemic, in which their Dark Soul would explode from their bodies and manifest as an amorphous black blob with bestial features which attacked anything with destructive ferocity. The infestation of these Pus of Man led to the permanent closure of the Grand Archives' doors, with the scholars isolating themselves from the desperate situation of the kingdom to continue their work.

title: Olaphis
snippet: When the First Flame began to fade during the reign of Olaphis, the undead began to appear. The undead curse was initially seen as a disease, and the "afflicted" were captured and locked up in the Bastille fortress in order to protect the land from the spreading curse. This limited measure wasn't sufficient to root out the cause, and the king of Olaphis became wracked with fear and suspicion. He started to see the progenitor of the curse in everything; gradually he rounded up every suspected carrier of disease, and the Bastille soon overflew with prisoners. The king seized any perceived threats and undesirables, cursed or no, and impounded them in the prison fortress, in an effort to keep unwanted things out of sight.

title: Ashen One
snippet: At this point in the game, Yoel of Londor will die. If the Ashen One has allowed him to draw out their true strength a sufficient number of times, Yoel will be replaced by Yuria of Londor, who attempts to sway the Ashen One into usurping the First Flame and becoming the Lord of Hollows.

title: The Deep
snippet: While the man-eater had fulfilled his duty and was no longer active, the ramifications of his stay in the Cathedral had become profound. Aldrich, through devouring humans and their Dark Souls, had accumulated an immense amount of darkness that fermented and degenerated, becoming dark dregs, a darkness beyond any natural limit. The Cathedral's sacred and peaceful body of water that once served for purification had consequently been infected, continuing to accumulate and stagnate filth to the point of becoming "the Deep" in its final form: an abyssal sea of rotten darkness. This dark pool became a cradle of repulsive life, which began to spawn ravenous insects and maggots that infested the corpses buried around the church and brought them back to life.The deacons of the Cathedral soon found themselves responsible with sealing away the horrors that rose from the Deep, to the point of needing grand stories to drive away the madness caused by these abominations. title: Frozen Eleum Loyce
snippet: After their King was consumed by Chaos, many of Eleum Loyce's faithful knights decided to follow him and put him out of his misery, as his orders were to eliminate each malformed terror that arose from the flame, and they would thus not hesitate even it were their own leader. Sir Fabian led the loyal knights straight into the depths of the Old Chaos to exterminate its terrors one last time, however the mission proved to be a failure and not one of the selfless knights returned. The souls of the knights were taken by Chaos and corrupted, leading them to lose all sense of purpose and being, left in them driven only by the urge of expuning any who might disturb the flames, even if they were former compatriots. With their armor charred and burnt black by fire and still burning in agony they remained as empty shells controlled by the Chaos alongside their once-proud king. However a few woeful suls were able to sneak back home guided by the last faint vestige of self.

title: Champion's Gravetender and Gravetender Greatwolf
snippet: They will only be relieved of their duty by the Ashen One, who finds their way to the bottom of the painting and challenges the duo to partake in the old turnament of the champion. Should they not do that, however, the fate of the page and wolf remains a mystery. All that is known is that the old champion's remains would find their way in the possession of Amnesiac Lapp during the collapse of the world into the Dreg Heap.

title: Demon (lore)
snippet: Alsanna, as the heiress to her Lord's wishes and in reverence of the apocalypse, devoted herself and the power of her Dark Soul to a ritual in the hopes of appeasing the raging flame. With the ivory gates opened, the land of Eleum Loyce grew cold and lifeless, turning into a frigid expanse, in an attempt to freeze Chaos along with the entire country. The remaining Knights of Eleum Loyce remained to watch over the Garrison Ward under the King's final orders to contain the Chaos, waiting patiently for a new leader strong enough to guide them into its depths, while Alsanna remained in prayer inside the Cathedral over the depths to continue the ritual. The Old Chaos was thus contained, albeit it corrupted the Ivory King and his knights, nevertheless remaining confined by Alsanna's tireless effort. Chaos was repressed until a Bearer of the Curse came along and destroyed the Burnt King and his corrupted Eleum Loyce knights, definitively eradicating the offshoots of Chaos from Drangleic.

title: Age of Dark
snippet: Through another questline, the player can cooperate with Yuria, a leader of the Sable Church of Londor, who urges the Ashen One to take the Flame for themselves, to usher in an Age of Dark; for the Sisters of the Sable Church were under the guidance of Kaathe. This is Ending 4: "The Usurpation of Fire", where the Flame is wrested by the Ashen One, who is to lead the Age of Man as the Lord of Hollows. By the time of *Dark Souls III*, the undead curse has been accepted by the people of Londor, who have come to view it as a blessing, and their Hollow form as the "true face of man".

title: Olaphis
snippet: In the meantime, Straid was enlightened through his research, allowing him to understand the relation between the First Flame and the Undead Curse, as well as the cyclical nature of their world in which kingdoms rose and fell concurrent with the waning Flame. Straid's power and knowledge became the subject of fear, and he was tricked into a trap, petrified and imprisoned in the Bastille. Since he had never taken apprentices, most of his wisdom was lost with him. The other sorcerers of Olaphis suffered dreadful persecution and were imprisoned as well. As the fortress of the Bastille reached full capacity, the king of Olaphis built an immense underground port and used the Flexile Sentries, monstrous creatures born from the fusion of a pair of serpentine beings, to cram prisoners into crude ships, sentenced to certain death at sea. Many prisoners sank with the ships, but a small number of survivors drifted to the south and settled down.

title: Lucatiel of Mirrah
snippet: After she contracted the curse of undeath, Lucatiel traveled to Drangleic as it was rumored that the cure could be found in this land. With time, she became certain that her brother must have come here too. Lucatiel later confides that she feels the curse is taking over her, and that her memories begin to fade away, starting with the oldest.

title: Primordial Serpents
snippet: During the events of *Dark Souls III*, when the First Flame was almost fading out, their fate or the number of their survivors is unknown.

title: Gwyn, Lord of Cinder
snippet: victory, unable to exterminate the demons or destroy the Bed of Chaos, and ended up retreating and only managing to banish the demons underground while enslaving some lesser demons who would become servants of the gods.

title: Humans
snippet: Despite the fact that all of this was for the sake of the Human race, some were opposed to the loyalty to Gwyn; he consequently went so far as to raise a young Dragon named Midir to combat the abyssal entities of the Ringed City. A few secretly wished for the sleeping princess Filianore to be awoken, and ruin cast upon the city, but such individuals are apparently few and far between in terms of open admittance. A race of beings called the White-faced Locust was risen from the Abyss to give sermons on the Dark, as they were kindred to Humans, but most were gluttonous and sought to feast on people instead.

title: Drangleic
snippet: In the lands outside of Drangleic, the legend spread that, with the help of souls found in the region, the Undead could save themselves from the curse, avoiding losing their humanity and remaining Hollow forever. For this reason, those who died and returned to life as undead came to the ruined kingdom beyond the mountains with the hope of avoiding their fate.

title: Man Serpent (Lore)
snippet: Their connection to Olaphis might be relevant to this mystery, as there's evidence of the kingdom's activity in the land that would become known as Tseldora, due to their use of brightstone in the creation of the Dispelling Rings, as well as the location of the Staff of Wisdom of their making. The site itself is of great importance to Seath the Scaleless, as many of his creations are found nearby, and it is said the iconic stones in the area were even once part of him. As the Man Serpents were closely tied to the pale being, it's possible evidence of their existence, or even simply the Flexile Sentries themselves, were discovered in the area, and tamed to serve a new leader and purpose.

title: Gods
snippet: The natives of the forest of Millwood worshipped an "Ethereal Oak", and the grounds of their lands from which it grew. The tree would later rot due to the dragon Midir's attempts to use it to heal himself of Abyss, and the people of Millwood moved to the Painted World of Ariandel.

title: The Deep
snippet: Proceeding into the Ringed City, home of the Dark Soul, the Ashen One will behold an Abyssal swamp, a seedbed for abominations of Dark. The presence of deep-blue crystals throughout the swamp indicate that it draws its source from the stagnation of the Deep, giving rise to creatures such as the White-faced Locusts. These oversized insects view humans as kin, and claim to have been born from the same Dark. However, their habits echo those of the Saint of the Deep: they feast on human flesh. It can be assumed that their "cannibalism" similarly serves to plunge human souls into the Deep, where they become the shackles that bind the world.

title: The Old Chaos
snippet: The king made some attempts to combat the Chaos, and his knights delved valiantly into the depths to exterminate the terrible things that dwelled there, but not one of them returned. Eventually, the Ivory King sensed the degradation of his soul and left Eleum Loyce. He traveled deep into the Chaos with his knights until he was devoured by the flames.

title: Carthus of the Sands
snippet: Consumed by power, Wolnir wished to outlive every other being in the world and sentenced his entire empire to death, slaughtering civilians and soldiers alike. The Catacombs of Carthus, an immense underground necropolis, were built to inter the bones of countless people and soldiers. High Lord Wolnir would then use necromancy to reanimate himself and control a skeleton army and empire, wishing to remain the last being. Following this, the Abyss would break out in the Catacombs of Carthus and Wolnir would fall into it. Experiencing the terror of true darkness, Wolnir would plead to the gods for the first time, and his holy sword along with his stolen sacred bracelets would come to comfort him. They prevented him from being wholly swallowed by the Abyss, which was barely contained in a magical artifact.

snippet:

The Chosen Undead thus challenged and killed her to obtain her powerful Lord Soul. The destruction of the original Flame of Chaos ended Izalith's misery, but it also marked the beginning of the end for the demons who, without the Bed of Chaos that had spawned them, became a dying race.

snippet: The Chosen Undead then heads towards Oolacile Township in search of Artorias and Dusk. title: Nashandra

Nashandra -  Dark Souls II - boss - lore 
 lore : Nashandra began her life as a small fragment of Manus, Father of the Abyss. When Manus was defeated, he was reborn as many fragments varying in sizes. Nashandra was the incarnation of her "father's" want, and thus began desiring what she did not have: power.

Nashandra travelled to the land of Drangleic, and set her sights on its powerful ruler, King Vendrick. Deciding to seduce Vendrick, Nashandra assumed a human form of unparalleled beauty and warned him of a supposed looming threat beyond the sea: the Giants. She convinced him to invade the land of the giants to claim their power, which Vendrick did successfully. Vendrick then made Nashandra his queen, and under their leadership, Drangleic entered into a Dark-like peace. The rulership of Drangleic however, was not enough to quell Nashandra’s want, and she desired an even greater power: the First Flame, which she intended to claim for herself by using Vendrick and the Throne of Want.

title: Dark Soul
snippet:
Dark Soul -  Dark Souls - item - capabilities 
 capabilities : Any fragment of the Dark Soul that separates from the original can be fueled by emotions and willpower, and increase its usable power, making it the most unique of the four Lord Souls.

Most notable of its functions is the power to animate life and raise sentient beings from the Abyss, for the Dark Soul is the only Lord Soul which is intrinsically tied to the Abyss, unlike the other forms of life that take energy from Souls. The main lifeform connected to it is the Human race, but lesser creatures are said to have also risen from the Dark, such as the White-faced Locust. The Dark Soul is also linked to the Dark Hand, and by extension, the art of Lifedrain. This is the legendary power of the fabled Dark Lord, used to gain humanity from others. The Darkwraiths used this power to steal Humanity from their victims.

The dragon correlation would explain the presence of the horns, and the connection to the Undead might give a clue to the corruption's origins. The soul of Manus was a "viscous, lukewarm lump of gentle humanity". When Manus' humanity went wild, he became a raving beast and began to emanate the Dark, giving birth to the Abyss. It's possible that the Pus of Man are humanities similarly gone wild.

title: The Deep
snippet: A glimpse into what an approaching Age of Deep would look like is provided with the Dreg Heap. At the close of the Age of Fire, all human realms have converged and piled up into this single point: an enormous heap of civilizations, blanketed by thin layers of ash, which was all that remained after the First Flame had consumed the world. Beneath this heap of ashen remains is the dwelling of Murkmen; abyssal humanoids that wield stagnated dark soul dregs as weapons. They are dissimilar to the humanity phantoms risen from Manus's Abyss, each of whom were unblemished and serene fragments of the Dark Soul. The Murkmen, on the contrary, are inelegant, lousy corruptions of humanity, whose stagnation is visible on the dark-blue hues of their bodies. Their attacks can unleash massive, uproarious dregs that ceaselessly pursue humanity—these are, after all, accumulations of stagnated humanities, looking to augment its darkness with each targeted soul.

snippet: Along with the "elite" Abyss Watchers, the complete Undead Legion consisted of two other levels. Due to the Legion's emphasis of speed over physical power, they asked the skilled sorcerer to develop unique variations of existing sorceries for the acolytes to use. At this point, the Watcher's sword will ignite, causing it to deal additional Fire damage and leaving trails in the floor that erupt into large pillars of flame. The Watcher himself will also take on an Embered appearance, revealing his true form as one of the Lords of Cinder.

The other Watchers no longer rise during the second phase, but the main Watcher is considerably more aggressive and powerful. The fight plays out in a similar fashion, but most of the Watcher's greatsword attacks are altered in some way. From the description of their soul and the ability to create the Wolf Knight's Greatsword, it seems that the massive soul of the Undead Legion is a reincarnation of Artorias himself, as many souls have been known to eventually reincarnate.
The design of the Abyss Watchers appears to be based on the Keeper of the Old Lords from *Bloodborne*.

title: Abyss Watchers
snippet:
Abyss Watchers -  Dark Souls III - boss - lead 
 lead : The **Abyss Watchers**, also known as the **Undead Legion of Farron**, are a collective boss in *Dark Souls III*, and are the first of the four main enemies that the Ashen One is tasked with slaying.

Found at the end of Farron Keep, the first phase of their boss battle is unusual: it involves a "main" Watcher whose health bar must be depleted, and who is joined as time passes by others with their own health bars, but also Watchers corrupted by the Abyss, who will indiscriminately target both the Ashen One and the uncorrupted Watchers, the latter of whom will fight back, turning the fight at times into a three-sided battle. Once the main Watcher's health is depleted, they regenerate for a second phase where they are the sole opponent.

title: Abyss Watchers
snippet:
Perhaps the most telling of their fall were the number of foot soldiers tasked with the covert disposal of corrupted members. As the Abyss slowly morphed the Legion's lost members, the so-called "Followers" would be sent to execute them before they were transformed into abyssal beasts. Their primary technique was to surround the target, burning and stabbing them, and finishing them with honor using javelins thrown with great force.

Beneath their home in Farron Keep are the Catacombs of Carthus, which contain a chalice holding High Lord Wolnir, who fell to the Abyss long ago. Along with the cindered Smouldering Lake, nearby is the Cathedral of the Deep, resting place of Aldrich, Devourer of Gods.

title: Abyss Watchers
snippet:
Abyss Watchers -  Dark Souls III - boss - description 
 description : The Abyss Watchers are a legion of troops that all wear a distinctive armor consisting of leather over chainmail, a long cloak, and a distinctive, pointed helm concealing a mask, seen as a sinister symbol by the masses. They are known for combating the Abyss wherever it may break out, and eradicating any of its abominations. They are believed to serve in the name of Artorias the Abysswalker, who was sworn to the same duty.

All of them use a greatsword and curved dagger. The dagger is not primarily used for offense, or even parrying, but as a hook for the Watchers to utilize their wild, unpredictable fighting style.

By the time the Ashen One encounters the Legion, they are mercilessly fighting one another, seemingly because some of the remaining Watchers have gone mad from exposure to the Abyss, hence their glowing red eyes.

title: Abyss Watchers
snippet:
Abyss Watchers -  Dark Souls III - boss - strategy 
 strategy : The fight consists of the player fighting a lone Abyss Watcher, who is present during the entire battle. More Abyss Watchers will awaken to join the battle as it progresses. These Watchers are much more fragile than the main Watcher, but they can still deal a considerable amount of damage, especially when multiple attack at once.

Every other Watcher that awakens, starting from the second, will be red-eyed and hostile toward other Watchers. They can directly attack the player or each other, but they will mostly focus on the other watchers. These Watchers can be used to the player's advantage, as they assist in dealing damage and taking aggro. As such, it may be a good idea to switch to a more defensive playstyle while the player waits for these Watchers to even out the odds.

title: Abyss Watchers
snippet:
Abyss Watchers -  Dark Souls III - boss - notes 
 notes : Can be parried, riposted and backstabbed in both phases of the encounter.
The Watchers wake up based on a timer. Damage dealt has an effect on how many of them are active.
All Watchers are instantly killed when the first phase of the fight is finished.
The Abyss-corrupted (red-eyed) Watchers are capable of finishing off the main Watcher. This has no direct effect on gameplay, however.
If an enemy followed the player up to the fog door, it may attract the corrupted Watcher's attention and he will keep trying to attack it for the rest of the first phase, rendering him unable to help against the others.
The Watchers that resurrect in the first phase of the fight are actually the same two Watchers, they will resurrect on the spot where they were killed.

title: Abyss Watchers
snippet:
Abyss Watchers -  Dark Souls III - boss - lore 
 lore : The Abyss Watchers were the main component of the Undead Legion of Farron, a special fighting force formed to combat the threat of the Abyss. Taking inspiration from the Wolf Knight (Sir Artorias, the Abysswalker), the Abyss Watchers themselves sought to utilize the techniques of Artorias, and partook of "wolf blood" to do so. Empowered by the legacy of Artorias, they became intensely strong and agile, fighting in a coordinated and sporadic pack akin to wolves.

title: Abyss Watchers
snippet: The main Watcher, although carrying a greatsword, is extremely fast and dexterous. He is constantly jumping around and evading the players swings by doing so. He will also try to take an advantage by swinging his greatsword around the floor of the arena. Never let your guard down, each and every attack can take you by surprise.

title: Abyss Watchers
snippet:
Though the Legion was not inherently evil or overtly violent, they quickly became known for their scorched-earth tactics, said to "bury" entire kingdoms at the first sign of exposure. Their distinct outfits, topped off with a tall, pointed helm, became an ill omen for its beholders. Their fighting style was enhanced by the revolutionary use of an ultra greatsword—modeled after Artorias' sword—along with a carved dagger, utilizing the dagger as support for utilizing their own unique, highly agile fighting techniques that was even more unpredictable and vicious than their predecessor. As such, they disdained the use of shields and preferred a constant offense.

The wolf's blood did more than enhance their bodies; the very essence of each Watcher who partook of the blood was interlinked, coalescing their souls into one. As such, instead of each body hosting distinct souls, all that partook the wolf blood shared the one soul, that of the "wolf blood master", distributed amongst them.

Covenant of Artorias -  Dark Souls - ring - general_information 
 general_information : Covenant of Artorias allows the player to reach the Abyss. As such, it is necessary in order to reach the Four Kings boss battle. Without wearing the ring, it is impossible to survive the fall into the Abyss. Taking off the ring during the fight with the Four Kings will cause the player to be devoured by the Abyss. Other than this, the ring has no other purpose.

The Covenant of Artorias is one of the very few rings that do not carry over to NG+; players are required to kill Great Grey Wolf Sif every playthrough to obtain the ring and beat the game. This ring, when dropped, will end up in the chest behind Kingseeker Frampt after the player has quit and reloaded the game. However, in the remaster, it will automatically be in the player’s inventory.

title: Covenant of Artorias
snippet: Once the player has defeated the Four Kings, the Abyss will cease killing the player in their world and the ring is no longer required to traverse it. title: Knight Artorias
snippet: In addition, Artorias and Sif had become trusted friends of Alvina, a white Great Feline that had lived for centuries since the early Age of Fire. title: Knight Artorias
snippet:
**Knight Artorias' pose in promotional artwork of Artorias of the Abyss DLC of Dark Souls eerily resembles Guts' own in his Berserker Armor as depicted in artwork of Voluma 28 of the *Berserk* manga series.
**Both are associated with enormous canines, though their dynamics contrasted greatly (Knight Artorias and Great Grey Wolf Sif were good friends, unlike Guts and Beast of Darkness whose relationship was antagonistic, true to the latter's nature as the former's personified rage and hatred).
**Knight Artorias's behavior and fighting style after being corrupted by the Abyss could be compared to Guts' own when the latter is completely under the influence of Berserker Armor.
